parts: Same painting. Three times. We changed only the color.
In red, the rainy street feels tense.
Claude Monet painted one cathedral front about thirty times. The stone never changed. The light did.
Van Gogh painted a café in red and green. He wrote to his brother that he wanted to show the terrible passions of humanity.
Science backs one part of this. In eighteen thirty nine, a chemist showed that the same grey looks different on red and on green. Documented.
Color changes what you see. What it does to your mood is much shakier.
Pink prison cells, painted to calm aggression. Did it work?
